name: Founding of Oxford University
summary: English scholars were expelled from the University of Paris around 1167, prompting a gathering of masters and students at Oxford. The town's existing tradition of teaching quickly grew into England's first university. Oxford developed the collegiate model of residential halls funded by endowments.

_quarry.structural_significance: Established the English tradition of residential collegiate universities; trained the ecclesiastical and civil administrators of medieval England.

sources_used: Catto (ed.), The History of the University of Oxford Vol. I
